title: Geometrical Compression with Preserved Local Rank Within Biological Solution Spaces
content: High-dimensional biological systems can be represented in fewer dimensions to achieve simpler descriptions of complex cellular and physiological data. However, compact organization is frequently interpreted as evidence of reduced underlying dimensionality. We introduce an approach to separate geometrical compression from loss of local mathematical degrees of freedom within a biological solution space. We built a synthetic system of interacting regulatory, metabolic and signaling states governed by nonlinear constraints and examined its admissible solutions across changes in a control parameter. Multistart root finding identified the possible states, while intersolution distances quantified their geometrical compression. In parallel, Jacobian singular values and condition numbers assessed local rank and sensitivity, with nearest-neighbor geometry, participation ratios and residual-gradient dynamics providing complementary information on solution organization and stability. Our analysis revealed progressive geometrical convergence of distinct solutions accompanied by increasing numerical sensitivity, while the Jacobian preserved full rank throughout the investigated range. This suggests that compression in state space can occur without a corresponding reduction in local mathematical degrees of freedom, providing a criterion for separating apparent low-dimensional organization from genuine local dimensional loss. Potential applications include identifying misleading low-dimensional representations, assessing whether compressed biological data preserve their original structure and detecting regions where model solutions become increasingly sensitive to perturbations.
